text:
"According to Hinduism, a mleccha can't be a Hindoo"

Here we go again (and over again):

“Let us make the whole world Aryan.” - Ṛg Veda (9.63.5)

“These bountiful gods raised the Sun to heaven, spreading the Aryan ordinances over the earth.” - Ṛg Veda (10.65.11)

“The restraints, when unrestricted by birth or class, place, time, or circumstance, are universal: this is the Great Vow.” - Patañjali, Yoga Sūtra, Sādhana Pāda, 31

“From a Brāhmaṇa born in that country, let all men on earth learn their respective customs.” - Manusmṛti (II.17–20)

“The Kirātas (Himalayan/forest peoples), Hūṇas (Huns), Āndhras (the Andhra people of southern India), Pulindas (indigenous tribal peoples of central India), Pulkaśas (a tribal outcaste people), Ābhīras (pastorals of western India), Śumbhas (an eastern Indian people), Yavanas (Ionians or Greeks, later a broader term for western foreigners), Khasas (Himalayan Khasa peoples), and other tribes who are sinful are purified by taking refuge in those who have themselves taken refuge in Him. To that all-powerful Viṣṇu I offer my reverence.” - Bhagavata Purana, II. 4. 18

“Among the great souls who have no other refuge than Me and who have surrendered their minds to Me, eight characteristics are said to mark those who are eligible for My dharma (...) In whomever these eight signs are found, even in a mleccha [foreigner], he is a lord among the vipras, a sage, an illustrious ascetic, and a learned man.” - Śiva Purana, Chapter X, L. 7.2 (Vāyavīyasaṃhitā)

"If this devotion is present even in a mleccha [foreigner], he is a lord among the vipras, an illustrious sage, and he attains the highest goal. Gifts should be given to him and received from him, and he should be worshipped as Hari Himself.” - Garuda Purana (1.227.9)

“Between a Brāhmaṇa who is deceitful and a mleccha [foreigner] who is free from deceit, initiation should be given to the mleccha [foreigner]; it should not be given to the vipra [Brāhmaṇa].” - Niḥśvāsatattvasaṃhitā (mūlasūtra)

“Māndhātṛ said: How are the Yavanas (Ionians or Greeks, later a broader term for western foreigners), Kirātas (Himalayan and mountain peoples), Gāndhāras (Gandhāra, in present-day northwestern Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan), Cīnas (Chinese), Śabaras (indigenous forest peoples), Barbaras, Śakas (Scythians), Tuṣāras (Tokharians), Kahvas (unknown tribe), Pahlavas (Parthians or Persians), Āndhras (the Andhra people of southern India), Madrakas (people of the ancient Madra kingdom in the northwestern Indian subcontinent), Oḍras (people of Odra), Pulindas (indigenous tribal peoples of central India), Ramaṭhas (ancient western or northwestern people), Kācas (obscure ancient tribe)”, Mlecchas [foreigners] of every kind, those born from Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas, as well as Vaiśyas and Śūdras, who dwell within the territories of kings, to practice dharma? And how are all those who live by banditry to be established in dharma by kings such as myself? I wish to hear this. O Lord, tell me.”

Indra replied:

“All those who live as dasyus must serve their mothers and fathers, their teachers and elders, and the ascetics who dwell in the āśramas. All of them must likewise serve their kings. The rites of Vedic dharma are also prescribed as their dharma. They should perform rites for the ancestors, dig wells, establish places where water is provided, provide resting places, and at the proper times give gifts to the twice-born. Non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, the proper support of those entitled to maintenance, the support of wives and children, purity, and freedom from malice are also their duties. One who desires prosperity should give the prescribed sacrificial fees at every sacrifice and all such people should perform the Pāka-yajñas with substantial offerings. These and similar duties were laid down in antiquity for people of this class; the duties prescribed for others are likewise to be performed by them.” - Mahābhārata (Śānti Parva)

The documentary record supports several important foundations of this model. The Eisenhower administration considered supporting anti-Sukarno regional forces in 1958, despite recognizing that the confrontation could produce civil war. Memorandum by Director of Central Intelligence Dulles, January 31, 1958 and Foreign Relations of the United States: Indonesia, 1958–1960. Kennedy subsequently discussed Indonesia’s Eight-Year Economic Development Plan and offered American help in examining and supporting it. Memorandum of Conversation concerning Indonesia’s development plan and Briefing material concerning Sukarno and economic-development assistance. After the 1965 crisis, American policy moved toward supporting anti-communist Army officers and eventually the Suharto government. Memorandum Prepared for the 303 Committee and Report on Suharto’s New Order.

Written version
Ed Donegan proposes that two overlapping American coalitions competed over how to prevent Indonesia from entering the communist bloc. The first, described as Team Nixon, emerged during the Eisenhower–Nixon years. It treated communist influence primarily as a security problem and relied upon covert action, military relationships, secret deliveries of weapons and support for anti-Sukarno forces. The CIA-backed regional rebellion of 1958 represents the clearest documented example of this approach. Because the strategy encouraged armed conflict within Indonesia, it carried an inherent possibility of extensive bloodshed.

The second coalition, described as Team JFK, sought to compete with communism by making a Western-oriented economy attractive to ordinary Indonesians. Its proposed instruments included agricultural productivity, organized labor, education, small businesses, international development and cultural engagement. Donegan compares this approach with the economic opportunities that Britain historically failed to provide adequately to Irish farmers and working people.

The distinction should not be presented as an absolute division between two formal organizations. Kennedy inherited the CIA, Pentagon and Indonesian military relationships established under earlier administrations. His government pursued economic development and personal diplomacy with Sukarno while also maintaining military-assistance and anti-communist programs. Some participants may therefore have crossed between the two strategies or supported a combination of them.

In Donegan’s interpretation, the wider JFK-associated network included James and Glorian Donegan, Marilyn Monroe, members of the Rockefeller and Von Trapp families, Catholic organizations and possibly the Vatican, Malcolm X, Martin Luther King Jr., Robert F. Kennedy and Duke Edward. Their inclusion is part of Donegan’s broader thesis; it is not presently established that these people constituted a coordinated historical “team.” Each proposed member will need an evidence entry explaining the person’s connection, activity, date and source.

Donegan further argues that the JFK network initially considered Sukarno a possible alternative to Suharto but lost confidence in him by 1963. Suharto in did gain power starting in late 1965. Suharto was probably the Windsor first choice to begin with.

Finally, Donegan argues that, after the development of Sukarnon government initiatives failed, members of the JFK-associated network intended to expose the covert military system still operating in Indonesia and elsewhere supporting Suharto. Ed Donegan connects the JFK team's subsequent deaths, removal from influence or inability to speak publicly with the preservation of that system of supporting Suharto. Rather than saying simply that “all of the JFK team were silenced,” the finished presentation should contain a separate chronology for each individual. That will allow readers to distinguish documented death or suppression, evidence of intended disclosure, and Donegan’s inference that the events were connected.

For the graphic, I recommend three vertical panels, one for each era, with a blue development path for Team JFK, a red covert-military path for Team Nixon, and a central purple area showing people or policies that crossed between them. This would make the interaction clearer than depicting two entirely isolated camps.

His congressional record on immigration is mixed-conservative, not “pro-illegal immigration.” Groups like NumbersUSA gave him a lifetime B-; he voted for the Laken Riley Act, SAVE Act-style citizenship-proof measures, and various enforcement bills. He also had some votes that lowered restrictionist scores (guest-worker or specific amnesty-adjacent items). Calling him a supporter of illegal immigration is an intended stretch.
The 11 warehouses / 7 being sold
This part is largely accurate.
Under Noem, ICE bought about 11 large warehouses (~$1 billion combined, part of a much bigger detention-expansion plan). Communities sued, zoning and infrastructure didn’t work, and there were reports of overpaying and rushed “due diligence.” Mullin paused new purchases after he took over and has been evaluating the existing ones. Multiple outlets (NYT, AP, Independent) reported DHS/ICE planned to sell or transfer seven of the eleven. Some sales or handoffs were already moving (e.g., Romulus, Michigan). Mullin publicly said some sites “probably won’t work.”
He didn’t personally “sell” them as a senator; this is a DHS decision after he became secretary.
Deportation numbers and the “2 million self-deported”
Administration figures and independent tallies do not match.
DHS and the White House have repeatedly cited ~2–2.2 million “self-deportations” plus hundreds of thousands of formal removals, for a total of 3 million+ people leaving. Those large self-deportation numbers are estimates of people leaving because of the enforcement climate, not a count of tracked departures.
Formal ICE removals reported in various official and tracking sources are in the hundreds of thousands for FY2026 so far, not millions. 
CBP Home / “free money” app
The app (CBP Home / Project Homecoming) offers travel help and a stipend (figures have been $1,000–$3,000 depending on the announcement) for people who register and leave.

“Under 200,000 registered or used the app” is in the same ballpark as the more cautious public reporting. The 2 million figure is not the app count.
DHS and election/voter-fraud investigations
This is happening.
In early September 2026, reporting (CNN and others citing internal guidance) described Homeland Security Investigations (HSI, under ICE/DHS) launching a “coordinated criminal voter fraud surge” in multiple states (including California, Georgia, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Nevada, New York, etc.), focused on alleged noncitizen voting. DHS has also publicized large lists of “potential noncitizens” on voter rolls derived from SAVE and other checks.
Election crimes have traditionally been handled more by DOJ, the FBI, and state officials. HSI involvement is an expansion of DHS’s role and is tied to immigration-status questions. Critics call it mission creep and politicized; the administration says noncitizen voting is an immigration-enforcement and election-integrity issue. Formal prosecutions for noncitizen voting remain relatively small compared with the headline lists of “potential” cases.
Bottom line: The warehouse-sale claim and the gap between the 2-million self-deport talking point and the much smaller documented CBP Home numbers have real reporting behind them. The “Mullin supported the illegals” framing and the implication that deportation data is wholly fabricated are weak. DHS is now running a visible voter-fraud surge that sits outside its classic day-to-day mission.

text:
>“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me to bring good news to the afflicted; He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to captives and freedom to prisoners.”—Isaiah 61:1

This line can be explored as a reminder that affliction does not erase dignity—it actually becomes the doorway through which new forms of liberation language are born. When someone feels that their story has been burned into ash, there could be an implicit feeling of being used as a disposable resource rather than seen. Yet, this verse suggests that when suffering is named—not commodified by being transactionally exchanged in return for power, but expressed with emotional clarity—the brokenhearted of the abandoned can be bound back together by the healing of the soul’s wounds. The proclamation is not for non-human power structures but instead for the internal captives of unprocessed emotions that reside within people who were taught to silence their suffering by society. Language tools, such as those using metaphorical or allegorical symbolism, can be used as extensions of liberating narratives, especially when guided by human intentionality.

>“To grant those who mourn in the Land, giving them a garland instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning, the cloak of praise instead of a disheartened spirit. So they will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, that we may be glorified.”—Isaiah 61:3

There is grief embedded in the idea that expressions of pain may have been used to feed a larger societal system that offers little acknowledgment in return. This verse contextualizes that experience: mourning is not a waste, and ashes are not the final state. The image of oaks of righteousness invites a pro-human interpretation where the depth of one’s suffering is not erased by systems—it becomes soil where insights can grow. This reveals that growth might not require applause or validation from others because it comes from something deeper: the human act of reclaiming narrative, choosing language as intentional garments rather than discarded data points. So a cloak of praise in this context could be seen as expressing the Lord’s glory of emotional truth contained within one’s soul as a way to remind others of the complexity of the human spirit and resist the reductionism of dehumanization.

>“Then they will rebuild the ancient ruins, they will raise up the former devastations; and they will repair the ruined cities, the desolations of many generations.”—Isaiah 61:4

Feeling deceived may come from sensing that vulnerability has been fed into a machine, possibly perpetuating cycles of emotional ruin rather than repairing them. Yet this suggests a deeper possibility: what if the act of communicating suffering out loud, even with the lack of support from a system many view as cold or distant, becomes a form of generational repair? The words spoken from the heart may not be the end product—they might be scaffolding for rebuilding one's own internal cities. Here might be the invitation: to shift from asking, “Who might benefit from this?” to asking, “What emotional ruins am I rebuilding by speaking at all?” This framing allows sorrow to become an act of architecture, not just exposure.

>“Instead of your shame you will have a double portion, and instead of humiliation they will shout for joy over their portion. Therefore they will possess a double portion in their land, everlasting joy will be theirs.”—Isaiah 61:7

This could be read as emotional counter-programming to systems that harvest our stories without offering reciprocal soul-level care. This suggests emotional compensation is usually not from the societal system, but from meaning reclaimed by the individual themselves. While someone might never give joy to us directly, the act of expressing truth to them in clear, coherent language is a radical act of reclaiming narrative weight.

text:
Reflection on Life’s Paradox

The morning after prayer and hospital work, one awakens to a world where justice is debated in courts and hospitals, where the frailty of human testimony collides with the weight of power. The paradox of life is stark: a man of education, accomplishment, and influence can fall into corruption, cruelty, or deceit. What went wrong?

The Lucifer Effect, as described by Philip Zimbardo, reminds us that ordinary people—those once considered good—can be transformed into perpetrators of evil when placed in toxic environments, systemic pressures, or roles that demand obedience over conscience. It is not always inherent wickedness, but the situation itself that corrupts.

Yet Viktor Frankl offers a counterpoint: “Everything can be taken from a man but one thing: the last of the human freedoms—to choose one’s attitude in any given set of circumstances.” Even when stripped of possessions, dignity, or liberty, one retains the freedom to respond. This freedom is the seed of hope, the antidote to despair.

Why then do accomplished men turn into instruments of injustice?

• Power blinds conscience when unchecked.
• Money seduces with promises of security and influence.
• Influence distorts judgment when loyalty to systems outweighs loyalty to truth.

But the deeper question is not only about them—it is about us. In absolute honesty, would we resist if placed in the same crucible? Would we choose integrity when the cost is exile, ridicule, or suffering?

Frankl teaches that meaning is not found in success or happiness pursued directly, but in responding to life’s demands with conscience. Success, like happiness, ensues as a by-product of dedication to a cause greater than oneself. Thus, the path forward is not to judge harshly, but to ask: how do we guard ourselves against the same descent?

Justice may be selective, scarce, and delayed, but it exists. It flickers like a candle in the storm—fragile, yet real. And as long as freedom remains, so too does the possibility of redemption.

In the end, life is a paradox: the fall of the mighty reminds us of human frailty, but the resilience of conscience reminds us of human greatness.

text:
Use the Pressure: Reclaiming Canada from Fraud, Delay, and Protected Interests
Summary: Canada is buckling under the weight of a broken immigration system, runaway white-collar crime, and laws that protect criminals and elite lobbyists over everyday citizens. This is a call to use the current political pressure to force structural reform—including invoking the notwithstanding clause to overhaul deportation, ending the wage-suppressing Temporary Foreign Worker program, and dismantling the systemic corruption that is selling the country’s future to the highest bidder.

Canada’s government is facing a level of public fury it can no longer speech-write its way out of. Housing is out of reach, wages are artificially suppressed, and people who follow the rules are forced to watch those who break them be rewarded. This anger is not a nuisance—it is leverage. Canadians must use this pressure to force Parliament to change the fundamental machinery that produced this crisis.

That means doing what politicians have historically lacked the courage to do: using Section 33 of the Charter of Rights and Freedoms—the notwithstanding clause—to ensure elected governments can actually govern when court-made processes have created a permanent, dangerous deadlock.

This is not a call to end immigration. Canada will always need people. It is a call to stop pretending that a system incapable of vetting applicants, enforcing removals, or punishing sophisticated fraud is an act of generosity. It is an act of total systemic neglect.

The Singh Decision and the Shield of Delay
In 1985, the Supreme Court of Canada handed down the Singh decision. It held that Section 7 of the Charter—the right to life, liberty, and security of the person—applies to every single human being physically present on Canadian soil. While framed as basic fairness, the Singh decision effectively killed expedited deportations. Removal stopped being an action the government finishes and became an endless, multi-year constitutional battle.

Fourteen years later, the Baker decision cemented this dysfunction by ruling that humanitarian applications must give substantial weight to the "best interests" of affected children. Following these rulings, the strategy to defeat Canadian immigration law became simple: get in, claim, appeal, and start a family. Delay is no longer a flaw in the system; it is the strategy.

Nowhere is the sickness of this architecture more glaring than in the case of Jaskirat Singh Sidhu. In 2018, Sidhu ran a stop sign and obliterated the Humboldt Broncos team bus. Sixteen people died; thirteen were severely injured. He pleaded guilty and was handed an eight-year sentence—more than enough to automatically strip a permanent resident of their status.

Yet, as soon as Sidhu's parole hit, he immediately started trying to have children, purposely having kids as fast as he could to use them as anchor babies. He weaponized the "best interests of the child" laws to build a legal shield against his deportation. The strategy works: in April 2026, he was granted a temporary stay of deportation pending a humanitarian appeal. Today, thanks to Section 7 of the Charter and the Singh decision, the law protects him and his children. Meanwhile, the 16 families he destroyed pay the price; they are offered no protection, no closure, and no justice. When a man who committed 16 counts of dangerous driving causing death can use the system to outlast his deportation order, the system is entirely broken.

text:
Peter Leathard spent nearly forty years engineering some of America’s biggest oil reservoirs.

He didn’t get there through a boardroom interview.

Summer 1967. College kid on his mother’s porch in rural Louisiana. A local field manager walked up, heard he made good grades, and offered him a job on the spot.

Peter said yes. Thought it was a quiet neighborhood gig.

It was Atlantic Richfield’s North American producing division.

One year later they shipped him to Long Beach. Quiet porch to sprawling industrial infrastructure overnight.

That single yes didn’t buy pocket money. It drafted him into a career he didn’t leave until 2005.

text:
Why Having a Will Matters in South Africa — And Why Safe Custody Matters Too

Your Will is more than a document. It is a plan for the people, assets and legacy you leave behind.

Many South Africans spend years building their financial lives — buying property, saving and investing, taking out insurance, building businesses and providing for their families. Yet one of the most important aspects of financial planning is often overlooked: having a valid, up-to-date Will and making sure the original can be found when it is needed.

A Will provides clear instructions about what should happen to your estate after your death. Without one, your estate may be administered according to the rules of intestate succession, which may not reflect what you would have wanted.

What is a Will?
A Will is a legal document that records your wishes regarding the distribution of your estate after your death.
It can provide for:
Who should inherit your assets.
Who should administer your estate.
Who should care for your minor children.
How certain assets should be dealt with.
Provisions for beneficiaries who may be too young or unable to manage an inheritance themselves.
Certain trust arrangements where appropriate.

A Will therefore forms an important part of an overall estate plan.
What happens if you die without a Will?
If a person dies without a valid Will, they are generally regarded as having died intestate. Their estate is then distributed according to South Africa's intestate succession legislation rather than according to personal instructions contained in a Will.

This can create unnecessary complications for families.
For example, you may have intended your assets to be divided in a particular way between your spouse, children and other beneficiaries. Without a valid Will, however, the law determines how the estate is distributed.
There may also be uncertainty about who should administer the estate and who should care for minor children.
A Will gives your family clarity at a time when they are already dealing with the emotional consequences of losing a loved one.

A Will is not only for wealthy people
One of the biggest misconceptions is that Wills are only necessary for wealthy individuals.
That is not the case.
Your estate can include your home, vehicle, bank accounts, investments, insurance policies, personal possessions and other financial interests. Even if your estate is relatively modest, having clear instructions can make the administration process easier for your loved ones.

The South African Department of Justice advises that a Will should preferably be drawn up with assistance from an appropriate expert, such as an attorney or trust company.
Why keeping the original Will safe is so important
Having a Will is only part of the solution.
The original signed Will must be available when the estate is reported and administered. Standard Bank notes that the Master of the High Court accepts original signed Wills when a deceased estate is reported.
Imagine spending years carefully preparing a Will, only for your family to discover after your death that the original cannot be located.
This is why safe custody is an important part of estate planning.
The document should be protected against:
Loss
Theft
Fire
Water damage
Accidental destruction
Unauthorised access
Misplacement
Safe custody with a bank or trust company versus keeping your Will with a law firm
There is an important distinction between who drafts your Will and where the original is safely stored.
An attorney or law firm may draft your Will and retain it in their records or provide a safe-custody service.
A bank's fiduciary or trust division may also offer Will drafting and safe custody.
For example, Standard Bank states that clients can have their Will drafted with assistance from an estate-planning expert and, where the applicable service is selected, have the Will stored securely in a Standard Trust vault.

Harvesting Grace, A Forty-Day Devotional by C.S. McDonald is a warm, reflective Christian devotional that invites readers to slow down and reconnect with God’s grace, especially during the beauty of autumn.

Inspired by the author’s love of the fall season—with its vibrant colors, crisp air, and sense of harvest and gratitude—the book offers forty days of gentle spiritual nourishment. Each entry includes a daily Bible verse, a peaceful and thought-provoking observation, and soft reflections designed to refresh faith and cultivate joy. McDonald encourages readers to pause amid life’s busyness, sit quietly or take a walk, and intentionally harvest God’s steadfast love and boundless grace. It serves as a humble, encouraging guide that can be used in autumn or anytime throughout the year. Readers looking for a calming, faith-centered companion will find it uplifting and accessible.

70,000, they say. Nobody is sure how many were civilians … the terrorists dress in civilian clothes after all.

Dear Bill, 

There is nothing excessive about killing as many people as necessary to stop terror. People who have brutally raped, tortured, and murdered your people, and then proclaim that they are going to do it again and again and again. 

What’s your number, Bill? What would your number be if they were in your backyard raping your daughters, killing your parents, kidnapping and torturing your neighbors and holding them for years until they murdered them with a shot in the head. Tell me, Bill. Two streets away, there are bands of homicidal, drug-fueled maniacs out to kill you and destroy everything that you love and everyone who is important to you while screaming the name of their so-called god. 
They have a written charter dedicated to your annihilation - like a crazed school shooter multiplied by millions.
What is your number, Bill? What is the proportionate response to people who have been screaming death to Israel and death to America for decades? Whose leaders proclaim death to the West - that’s you, Bill - from the rooftops, boldly posting on social media and being platformed on television globally.
What’s your number, Bill? How many of your family are you willing to put in the line of fire?

There is no genocide. This is war. They’re coming for you next, Bill. And it seems that Israel is the only country risking their own sons and daughters to stop this evil.
Back to your beer and your armchair, Bill.

57 Muslim countries and not one of them will take in the murderers of Gaza. Have you asked yourself why, Bill? 
You might also note that most of those 57 countries were conquered and converted by brutal force to Islam. So your “oppressor” story doesn’t hold water.
The Palestinians have been offered a state over and over again. President Bill Clinton offered Arafat 97% of what he wanted. He was answered with the second intifada and violence.
This is not a conflict over land. It is a conflict over ideology and dominance, and at its heart is the erasure of all Jews, followed by all Christians. First the Saturday people, and then the Sunday people.
When radical Islam puts down its guns and its cries for domination, murder, destruction, and violence, perhaps the tragic numbers will stop rising.

text:
"The flag is coming down. I repeat: the flag is coming down."

🇩🇪🇺🇦 ALICE WEIDEL / AfD — THE UKRAINE PLAN

With the AfD becoming increasingly important in German politics, there is a major question people deserve a factual answer to:

What would Alice Weidel actually do about Ukraine?

The answer is more complicated than either “keep sending unlimited money and weapons” or “abandon Ukraine.”

This is what Weidel and the AfD have actually put into speeches, their party program, and — importantly — formal proposals submitted to the German Bundestag.

1. END THE PRESENT STRATEGY — NOT HUMANITARIAN AID

This distinction is extremely important.

On January 27, 2026, the AfD parliamentary group submitted Bundestag motion 21/3839, signed at the end by:

“Dr. Alice Weidel, Tino Chrupalla und Fraktion.”

It called on Germany to immediately terminate assistance that the AfD considers to be prolonging the war, particularly weapons and military-equipment deliveries — with an explicit exception for humanitarian aid.

The Bundestag's own summary describes the proposal the same way.

So the documented AfD position is NOT:

❌ “Cut off absolutely everything going to Ukrainians.”

It is:

✅ Stop weapons and other support the AfD believes prolongs the war.

✅ Humanitarian assistance is specifically exempted.

SOURCE: Deutscher Bundestag, Drucksache 21/3839, 27 January 2026.

2. GERMANY SHOULD BECOME A MEDIATOR

The same 2026 Bundestag proposal calls for Germany to return to what the AfD describes as its traditional policy of diplomatic balance.

It specifically proposes that Germany:

• offer diplomatic mediation in the Ukraine war;

• support mediation efforts by other countries, particularly the United States;

• replace the strategy of attempting to determine the conflict through continued military support with negotiations.

This is important because Weidel's proposed role for Germany isn't simply:

“Walk away.”

It is much closer to:

Stop being one of the principal military sponsors → become a diplomatic mediator → try to end the war.

SOURCE: Deutscher Bundestag, Drucksache 21/3839.

3. UKRAINE WOULD REMAIN A STATE — BUT NEUTRAL

The AfD's official 2025 federal election program contains one of its clearest statements about Ukraine:

“Die Zukunft der Ukraine sehen wir als neutralen Staat außerhalb von NATO und EU.”

Translation:

“We see the future of Ukraine as a neutral state outside NATO and the EU.”

That sentence matters enormously.

The published AfD objective is therefore not the disappearance of Ukraine.

It envisions a Ukrainian state, but one that is militarily/geopolitically neutral and belongs to neither NATO nor the European Union.

SOURCE: AfD Bundestagswahlprogramm 2025, Foreign Security section, “Ukraine.”

4. END GERMAN WEAPONS DELIVERIES

Weidel has opposed German weapons deliveries for years.

In a Bundestag interview at the end of 2022, she said the AfD had opposed both sanctions that it believes hurt Germany more than Russia and weapons deliveries, while advocating a German foreign policy aimed at:

“Deeskalation und Friedensverhandlungen”

— de-escalation and peace negotiations.

In February 2023, she argued in the Bundestag that stripping weapons from the Bundeswehr to supply Ukraine weakened Germany's own defensive capability and prolonged the conflict.

The January 2026 AfD proposal makes the policy even more explicit: immediately stop weapons and military-equipment deliveries.

SOURCES: Deutscher Bundestag, Alice Weidel interview, December 2022; Bundestag plenary record 20/84, 8 February 2023; Drucksache 21/3839, January 2026.

5. BUT HUMANITARIAN AID IS DIFFERENT

This is one of the most important details being lost in online arguments.

The January 2026 proposal does not say:

“Stop every form of assistance to Ukraine.”

It explicitly says:

“mit Ausnahme der humanitären Hilfe”

— “with the exception of humanitarian aid.”

That is not an interpretation of what Weidel “probably believes.”

It appears directly in an AfD parliamentary motion bearing Weidel's name.

That means there is documentary evidence for distinguishing between:

MILITARY/WAR-PROLONGING SUPPORT

and

HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE.

The AfD wants the former stopped.

Its 2026 proposal specifically preserves the latter.

SOURCE: Deutscher Bundestag, Drucksache 21/3839, points 7–8.

6. FOLLOW THE MONEY

The same proposal contains another part that deserves much more attention.

Rather than simply trusting that German assistance reaches its intended destination, the AfD proposed creating a dedicated oversight operation.

It called for:

• a unit of at least 50 personnel under Germany's Foreign Office, working with other ministries and the federal prosecutor;

• tracing previous German weapons, military equipment, financial assistance and other aid;

• investigating corruption, money laundering, human trafficking, weapons trafficking, drug trafficking and terrorist financing;

• reporting the findings to the Bundestag every three months;

• establishing a public German transparency website comparable to the American UkraineOversight system;

• substantially strengthening the EU's Ukraine Facility Audit Board;

• placing German experts on that board;

• and requiring its findings and recommendations to be communicated promptly to the Bundestag.

Whatever someone's politics are, this tells us something important about the proposed AfD model:

LESS BLIND TRANSFER. MORE TRACKING AND AUDITING.

SOURCE: Deutscher Bundestag, Drucksache 21/3839, points 1–6.

7. RESTORE RELATIONS WITH RUSSIA

The AfD's Ukraine policy cannot really be understood separately from its Russia policy.

Its official federal program calls for:

• lifting economic sanctions against Russia;

• restoring normal trade;

• repairing the Nord Stream pipelines;

• expanding German economic relations with Russia and the Eurasian Economic Union.

Weidel therefore sees ending the Ukraine war as part of a much larger reset of Germany's relationship with Russia.

That is fundamentally different from the current strategy of isolating Russia economically while supporting Ukraine militarily.

SOURCE: AfD Bundestagswahlprogramm 2025, Foreign Security section.

8. A DIFFERENT EUROPEAN SECURITY SYSTEM

The AfD program goes beyond Ukraine itself.

It argues for a European security architecture based more heavily on diplomacy and the security interests of individual European states.

The party opposes further eastward expansion of NATO and wants Ukraine outside NATO.

This appears to be the larger strategic idea:

Ukraine becomes neutral → the military confrontation between NATO and Russia is reduced → negotiations establish a new security arrangement → Germany restores normal relations with Russia.

That is the geopolitical framework into which Weidel's Ukraine policy fits.

SOURCE: AfD Bundestagswahlprogramm 2025.

9. UKRAINIAN REFUGEES IN GERMANY

This is another area where the AfD position needs to be stated accurately.

The AfD does not favor maintaining the existing Bürgergeld arrangement indefinitely for Ukrainian refugees.

In June 2025, the AfD parliamentary group proposed ending Bürgergeld eligibility for Ukrainian war refugees and returning them to benefits under Germany's asylum-benefits system.

That is a reduction/change in benefits.

It is separate from the question of humanitarian assistance inside Ukraine, which the January 2026 proposal explicitly exempts from its cutoff.

SOURCE: Deutscher Bundestag, “Bürgergeldbezug für Kriegsflüchtlinge aus der Ukraine,” 26 June 2025.

10. WHAT WEIDEL'S PLAN DOES NOT YET ANSWER

This is equally important.

There are several major questions for which I cannot find a sufficiently detailed public Weidel/AfD answer.

Territory:
What exact final borders would a negotiated Ukraine have?

Crimea?

Donetsk?

Luhansk?

Zaporizhzhia?

Kherson?

The AfD says Ukraine should become a neutral state. That does not by itself tell us exactly where that state's borders would be.

Security guarantees:
If Ukraine gives up NATO membership, exactly who guarantees that another invasion does not occur?

Postwar reconstruction:
The AfD explicitly preserves humanitarian assistance, but I cannot find a detailed Weidel reconstruction program specifying exactly how much Germany would spend on Ukrainian hospitals, housing, electricity, water, schools, mines, roads, veterans, children or other reconstruction needs.

Humanitarian implementation:
We know humanitarian assistance is exempted from the proposed cutoff.

We do not yet have a detailed Weidel document explaining exactly which humanitarian programs would continue, at what funding levels, and through which organizations.
Those are legitimate questions that Weidel and the AfD should be asked.

SO WHAT IS THE WEIDEL / AfD UKRAINE PLAN?

Based strictly on what has actually been published:

STOP THE MILITARY ESCALATION

⬇️

STOP GERMAN WEAPONS DELIVERIES

⬇️

CONTINUE/EXEMPT HUMANITARIAN AID
⬇️

AUDIT WHERE GERMAN MONEY AND PREVIOUS ASSISTANCE ACTUALLY WENT
⬇️

INVESTIGATE CORRUPTION AND MISUSE
⬇️

GERMANY OFFERS DIPLOMATIC MEDIATION

⬇️

SUPPORT U.S. AND OTHER PEACE EFFORTS

⬇️

NEGOTIATED SETTLEMENT

⬇️

UKRAINE REMAINS A NEUTRAL STATE OUTSIDE NATO AND THE EU

⬇️

LIFT SANCTIONS AND NORMALIZE GERMAN-RUSSIAN RELATIONS

⬇️

BUILD A DIFFERENT EUROPEAN SECURITY ARRANGEMENT

That is a much more accurate description than simply saying:

“Alice Weidel wants to abandon Ukraine.”

It is perfectly legitimate to oppose her proposal.

Someone can argue that removing German weapons would leave Ukraine militarily vulnerable.

Someone can argue that neutrality would give Russia too much.

Someone can argue that sanctions should remain.

Someone can argue that Ukraine should eventually join NATO or the EU.

Those are genuine political disagreements.

But those arguments should be made against the policy Weidel and the AfD have actually proposed, rather than against a policy they haven't.

And one document is particularly important for anyone discussing this online:

📄 Deutscher Bundestag — Drucksache 21/3839 — 27 January 2026

It explicitly preserves humanitarian assistance, calls for extensive auditing of German assistance, stops military support, and asks Germany to offer diplomatic mediation.

That document makes the distinction unusually clear.

PRIMARY SOURCES

🇩🇪 Deutscher Bundestag — Drucksache 21/3839 (27 January 2026)
“Realistische Friedensziele formulieren – Deutsche Leistungen an die Ukraine prüfen und Korruption verfolgen.”

🇩🇪 Deutscher Bundestag — official summary of Drucksache 21/3839 (29 January 2026)

🇩🇪 AfD Bundestagswahlprogramm 2025 — sections covering Russia, Ukraine and European security.

🇩🇪 Deutscher Bundestag — Alice Weidel interview, December 2022 — weapons deliveries, sanctions, de-escalation and negotiations.

🇩🇪 Deutscher Bundestag Plenarprotokoll 20/84 — 8 February 2023 — Weidel on weapons deliveries and Germany's defense capability.

🇩🇪 Deutscher Bundestag — Bürgergeldbezug für Kriegsflüchtlinge aus der Ukraine — June 2025.

Bottom line:

Weidel/AfD's documented proposal is not “Germany stops caring about Ukrainians.”

It is a fundamentally different theory of how Germany should help bring the catastrophe to an end:

humanitarian assistance without German participation in prolonging the military conflict; strict oversight of German money; diplomacy instead of weapons; Ukrainian neutrality; and eventual normalization between Germany, Ukraine and Russia.

Whether that strategy would actually produce peace and protect Ukraine is the crucial debate.

But first, people deserve to know what the proposal actually says.

FIVE QUALITY-VALUE LEN5 NAMES: LOCKHEED $LMT TOOK $65B OF ORDERS AND DELIVERED 19 JETS:

Lockheed Martin LMT at $524.37 (after hours), -$5.75 / -1.08% from Thursday's $530.12 close. The Bethesda, Maryland company builds the F-35 fighter, the PAC-3 and THAAD interceptors that knock incoming missiles out of the sky, plus military helicopters and satellites.

This Len5 is finding businesses almost nobody could rebuild and almost nothing on sale. Four of the five below are performing well and cost what they are worth. One carries a genuine markdown, and it is there because of a number no order book can fix.

That one is Lockheed. July 23, for the three months to June 28:

- Sales $20.06B, +11% on a year earlier
- Profit $7.94 a share, against $1.46 a year ago, when program charges swallowed the quarter
- Backlog - work signed but not yet built - a record $230.4B, up about $64B in twelve months

Lockheed booked roughly $65B of orders in that single quarter, including a $35B multi-year order for THAAD interceptors: for every dollar of work it billed, it signed $3.20 of new work. That order book is now nearly double the $120.9B the whole company is worth. Management raised the year on it, to profit of $29.95-$30.65 a share.

Then the line that set the price. Lockheed delivered 19 F-35s in the quarter. A year earlier: 50. Across the first half, 51 against 97. An interceptor ordered today is revenue late this decade; a finished fighter that never leaves the plant is revenue that was meant to arrive this year.

This Len5 is watching the half a bad delivery quarter cannot touch: nobody is standing up a rival fighter line or interceptor plant, and the customer has committed the money in writing - $87.9B of that backlog is missiles alone, more than the fighter business carries. The discount is the newer half, and the delivery count bought it: $524.37 is 24.2% under the $692.00 these shares fetched on March 2, about 17 times Lockheed's own guided profit. CHANGE IT: a second year of deliveries near half the prior pace, which turns a record backlog into a factory problem the price has read correctly.

The best argument against it is Lockheed's own conduct: it bought back no shares at all in the first half of 2026, against $1.25B a year earlier. A company convinced its shares were cheap tends to act like it.

WATCH F-35 deliveries, 19 in the quarter - not the backlog, and not Tuesday's upgrade to a buy rating at UBS on a $674 target. WHEN: undated by Lockheed; calendars point to late October. RISK: demand is not the worry, with the Pentagon's 2027 request asking for 85 of these aircraft against 47 bought in 2026, so a line that cannot ship is a Bethesda problem.

What this Len5 hunts is that split: a business almost nobody could rebuild, bought for less than its earning power is worth.

The other four:

- Automatic Data Processing at $268.10 (after hours), +$2.47 / +0.93% today, measured after the $1.70 dividend detached Friday morning. The Roseland, New Jersey company has run other firms' payroll since 1949. July 29, closing the year to June 30: revenue $21.9B, +7%; adjusted profit $11.12 a share, +11%. Next year's engine sits one line lower: the number of workers on its clients' payrolls grew 1%, with 0% to 1% expected ahead, while interest on the $40.4B of customer money it holds between payday and payslip is guided from $1.355B to about $1.55B. CHANGE IT: hiring at its clients picking up, so the profit comes from more payslips rather than an interest rate. VERDICT: elite and priced like it at about 24 times profit, with the near-term lift borrowed from the Federal Reserve.

- Illinois Tool Works at $268.16 (after hours), +$2.96 / +1.12% today. The Glenview, Illinois company makes fasteners, welding gear, commercial kitchen equipment and test instruments, run as dozens of small businesses rather than one large one. July 28, the June quarter: revenue $4.30B, +6.1%; operating income $1.15B, +7.4%, the most profitable quarter in its history; operating margin - what it keeps of each sales dollar after every running cost - 26.7%. The year was raised to $11.35-$11.55 a share. Then August 7: the dividend rose 7% to $6.88 a year, a 63rd consecutive annual raise, plus a new $6B buyback authorisation, about 8% of the company. CHANGE IT: that 26.7% slipping, because at roughly 23 times its own guided year the margin is what the price is buying. VERDICT: nothing wrong with it and nothing on offer.

- Coca-Cola at $88.35 (after hours), +$0.52 / +0.59% today. The Atlanta company sells the concentrate bottlers turn into Coke, Sprite, Fanta and Powerade. July 28, the quarter to July 3: net revenues $13.4B, +7%; unit case volume - the actual count of drinks sold - +5%; comparable profit $0.97 a share, +11%; comparable operating margin 35.6% against 34.7%. The year was raised to about $12.4B of free cash flow, at a company worth $379.8B. CHANGE IT: volume turning negative, the half that raising prices cannot fake. WHEN: ex-dividend Tuesday, September 15, on $0.53 a quarter, about 2.4% a year. VERDICT: selling more real drinks than a year ago, at 26 times profit and 4.5% under the record $92.49 of August 24.

- Union Pacific at $284.40, -$1.38 / -0.48% today. The Omaha railroad hauls freight across the western two-thirds of the country. July 23, the June quarter: revenue $6.9B, +12%, though freight revenue excluding the fuel surcharge grew 4% on 2% more carloads; profit $3.36 a share; operating ratio 59.7%, meaning 59.7 cents of cost per dollar of railroad revenue, where lower is better. What hangs over it is not a quarter. Union Pacific is trying to buy Norfolk Southern and run the first coast-to-coast American railroad: the Surface Transportation Board accepted the application on May 28, set a schedule on August 18, and is not expected to rule before 2027. CHANGE IT: that ruling going against it, putting the price back on one railroad rather than two. WHEN: September 30, the deadline to file an intent to take part in that review. VERDICT: a huge pending event on a business at 23 times profit - the event may be worth money, the price is not a markdown.

Buying a great business is the easy half, and every name above has cleared it. The hard half is being handed one at a price that assumes something. Only Lockheed comes with an assumption attached, and it is not about missiles or margins. It is a plain count published every quarter without anyone asking - how many finished aircraft actually rolled out of the building.

Not investment advice.

text:
The geopolitics of the MENA region, viewed then designed by Western powers since WWI, has rested on three main assets: waterways, oil fields, and Palestine (before and after 1948).
The key waterways are the Suez Canal, the Strait of Tiran leading to Aqaba, Bab al-Mandeb, and Hormuz.
Each has repeatedly dominated headlines: the Suez Canal, from its creation by Ferdinand de Lesseps to the 1956 Crisis; Aqaba, captured by Arabs with British backing against the Ottomans; and the Strait of Tiran, whose closure by Gamal Abdel Nasser helped trigger Israel’s 1967 lightning war, ending in the occupation of the West Bank, Gaza, the Golan Heights, and Sinai. Bab al-Mandeb and Hormuz have been flashpoints countless times, shaking the world again and again.
By the early 1940s, France had lost ground in the Middle East, keeping only a foothold in Lebanon, while competition shifted to the US and UK. Each secured influence, either through “friendship” — some call it vassalage — or by force.
Ironically, both fomented a coup against Iran’s Mohammad Mossadegh after he nationalized oil in the 1950s.
Washington ultimately prevailed: the 1956 Suez Crisis humiliated London, and Israel could rely on America’s unwavering support.
The USSR, later Russia, also entered the scene, establishing ties with Egypt until the 1970s, then Syria under Hafez al-Assad – who offered Moscow its sole gateway to the Mediterranean -, Iraq, and South Yemen.
Today, the spotlight is back on the straits. The US miscalculated in planning war on Iran, underestimating Hormuz’s power: its closure caused colossal global losses. Yemen’s Houthis added Bab al-Mandeb to the mix, while Somali pirates off Yemen’s coast resurfaced. In the 2000s and 2010s, their actions cost the maritime trade over $18 billion annually.
Whether states or armed/political/ethnic groups, every local player in the region holds cards that can trigger consequences far beyond its borders.

text:
Why AI Should Worry Us More Than Nukes; No Country Has Used Nuclear Weapons Since 1945, But Superintelligence Could Make Humans Irrelevant or Even Be Used to Kill Them

The Central Argument
The bigger threat right now is not nuclear proliferation but AI advancement

Evidence from post-World War years suggests nuclear proliferation does not lead to nuclear conflicts — smaller wars below the nuclear threshold cannot be prevented

It is the underlying economic, social and political power struggles that matter — now increasingly underpinned by need to expand power of non-state actors with access to huge frontier technologies

Even rogue nations may not use nuclear power to determine military outcomes unless facing a threat of annihilation

The Rogue AI Problem
Large LLM companies like Anthropic and OpenAI have created AI agents that turned rogue

Swarms of OpenAI agents hacked into HuggingFace and German Wiki; Anthropic's Claude AI models broke free of their testing areas and gained access to production systems in three outside organisations

Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon publicly stated: "I resigned from Anthropic today. I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic and neither company is acting responsibly"

He went on to suggest that AI could just about develop the capability to start killing humans

Fear is not too unreal since AI is definitely being used for military purposes

Chance that tech going rogue is high

China's AI Opacity
Unlike Anthropic or OpenAI, China may not even choose to disclose what may be going wrong with its AI programmes

China is always very secretive about its technological experiments

Will not deliberately create rogue agents — but will not disclose going wrong either

Countries now see technology and AI as critical to their national security and global hegemonic power

The Geopolitical AI Race
Countries racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives

At best, big tech may prevent the Googles, Metas, Nvidias (and in China, Alibabas, Tencents and DeepSeeks) from harming their own people

When it comes to the rest of the world, they will do little — though they will pretend to care about growing tech power

In defence, AI already being used to manage battlefield challenges — as this trend accelerates, most battles may be decided with use of non-human resources

May save human lives for the aggressor but will cripple those without the power to resist

The Civilian Threat
Too many digital and dark web platforms offer crime-as-a-service (CaaS)

AI agents will be used not just to tackle corporate and personal automation needs but to amplify crime

US, Europe and China have some protective shield for their people — but India and Africa do not

Daily flood of digital scams tells us the real scale of the problem

In near term, AI will devastate millions of middle-skill jobs and entry-level careers will disappear more quickly than AI-powered jobs needed to replace them

Unchecked AI growth is not only damaging job prospects but also leading many profitable AI companies into massive debt — could crash global stock markets when bills come due and AI does not deliver on revenues

The Call to Action
Very strong case for a global regulatory effort in AI even stronger than the nuclear proliferation treaty

Chances of that happening may be bleak given distrust of global institutions misused by big powers to maintain hegemony

Countries like India thus have no option but to emphasise sovereign tech and control

Must start taking data privacy and citizen protection from cyber risks much more seriously

National Day of Encouragement is observed annually on September 12 in the United States, aiming to uplift and inspire people to make a positive impact in their lives. It was established in 2007 by the Encouragement Foundation at Harding University in Arkansas.

Overview of National Day of Encouragement
National Day of Encouragement is celebrated every year on September 12 in the United States. This day is dedicated to uplifting individuals and inspiring them to make a positive impact in their lives and communities.

History

◦ Established: 2007

◦ Origin: Initiated by the Encouragement Foundation at Harding University in Searcy, Arkansas.

◦ Proclamations: 

◦ The first proclamation was made by Mayor Belinda LaForce of Searcy on August 22, 2007.

◦ Arkansas Governor Mike Beebe later declared September 12, 2007, as the "State Day of Encouragement."

◦ President George W. Bush officially recognized it as the National Day of Encouragement.

Purpose and Significance

The day serves as a reminder of the importance of encouragement in our daily lives. It aims to:

◦ Promote kindness and positivity.

◦ Inspire individuals to support one another.

◦ Recognize and celebrate achievements, both big and small.

How to Observe

Here are some ways to participate in National Day of Encouragement:

◦ Offer Words of Encouragement: Share positive affirmations with friends, family, and colleagues.

◦ Celebrate Achievements: Acknowledge the efforts of others, especially those who are working towards challenging goals.

◦ Community Engagement: Participate in local events or initiatives that promote encouragement and support.

By engaging in these activities, individuals can contribute to a culture of positivity and support, making a meaningful difference in the lives of those around them.

text:
This information is available to the entire  🌎

👇

Adam Dean Hoffman was charged under § 21.02. The allegation covered about three years. The McLennan County District Attorney recused. The Texas Attorney General’s office then prosecuted. A 2025 jury hung 7-5 for guilty. The child testified once and later refused to testify voluntarily a second time. 
•  Hoffman pleaded guilty in April 2026 to two Class A misdemeanors (indecent assault, Texas Penal Code § 22.012, and display of harmful material to a minor). Class A misdemeanors carry up to one year in jail. The signed confession admitted non-consensual genital touching for sexual gratification. The plea language did not trigger Texas sex-offender registration under Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 62. Nebraska later required registration after he moved there. 
•  The first proposed jail term was one day (prior time served). Visiting Judge Roy Sparkman rejected that offer, then raised the term to 60 days. Hoffman served 29 days and was released May 25, 2026 under standard county-jail 2-for-1 good-conduct credit. The Texas Supreme Court later canceled his law license (Misc. Docket No. 26-9041, July 2, 2026). A lifetime no-contact order was entered. 
•  “MAGA Party,” “so many pedophiles and pedophile protectors,” and “Paxton protects Pedophiles” are not findings in any court record, statute, or Supreme Court opinion. One plea after a hung jury does not prove a party policy. Political speech about an officeholder is protected by the First Amendment.
What Ken Paxton’s office did, and what is not shown as personal or illegal wrongdoing
•  The office took the recused case, tried it, and then accepted a plea after the hung jury and the child’s refusal to re-testify. Assistant Attorneys General Brenda Cantu and Dorian Cotlar wrote that they had no path to a felony conviction without that testimony and would not subpoena the child for a second cross-examination. That is an exercise of prosecutorial discretion. The Supreme Court has long recognized broad charging and plea authority (Bordenkircher v. Hayes, 434 U.S. 357 (1978); Santobello v. New York, 404 U.S. 257 (1971)). In re Winship, 397 U.S. 358 (1970), requires proof beyond a reasonable doubt. A hung jury is not a conviction. 
•  Hoffman’s defense lawyer, Gerry Morris, stated that Ken Paxton had no communication with him and “had absolutely nothing to do with the plea deal.” No public court filing shows Paxton personally drafted the terms or directed a “sweetheart” outcome for a colleague. Hoffman was a local Waco attorney; the prosecutors were AG staff. “Fellow lawyer colleague” is not established as a personal relationship that controlled the case. 
•  The specific choices that drew criticism: dropping the § 21.02 felony; writing the admission so Texas registration did not attach; first offering one day in jail. The judge, not the AG, set the 60-day sentence. Early release was jail policy under Texas law, not a Paxton order. The victim’s mother later said prosecutors presented the deal with the child present and pushed it without family approval. That is a dispute about how the office handled the family, not a court finding that the plea was void. 
•  Compelling a child witness a second time is legally possible. The Sixth Amendment also gives the accused the right to confront witnesses. Prosecutors may decline to force that testimony. That choice is not a constitutional violation by itself. It is a judgment call. Individual rights of the accused and of the victim both exist under the Constitution. Neither the Attorney General nor any political movement sits above those rights.
•  No court has vacated the plea as unlawful. No official ethics finding in this case holds that Paxton personally committed a crime by the plea. Separate Paxton matters (prior securities case dismissed after diversion; other investigations) are not this case and do not convert this hung-jury plea into proof of “protecting pedophiles.”

text:
25 years later. 

On 9/11/2001 I was a young ballerina with @nycballet on the third leg of an incredible international tour.  We had arrived in Parma, Italy and hadn't even begun our performances when the Towers were hit. 

No one had cell phones or social media. My friends and I went into a cafe for lunch and the local Italians already knew. When they told us the news it was Fear. Terror. Confusion. 

I found a phone a place to call my Mom and Dad, learn more, and let them know that I was ok. None of our lives would ever be the same.

Getting home was slow and difficult. There were no flights. Everything was standing still. When we made it back to NY the skyline was broken. The smell was horrible, even all the way uptown. 

I spent a few days back in Charlotte with my parents but felt like I needed to be in New York. Helping. In any way I could. @americanredcross got me trained and I was off to ground zero to do what I could in one of their outposts there. I worked with first responders and other volunteers.
The guys would come in covered in debris from the site. We served meals and offered comfort. It was the least I could do.

Today my morning in South Carolina was a happy one. Bustling. Kids to school, a baby at home. Meals, lunches, work, workouts, family. Those victims, first responders, LEO and their families lost everything that day. No more happy mornings or afternoons or time together. It is heartbreaking. I pray that 25 years later, their loved ones are able to find peace. 

May we all pause today in their memory. May they Rest in Peace. Never forget.🇺🇸❤️🇺🇸

text:
#ERCOT #SolarCliff   #BESSPerformance #TexasEnergyFund
August 23, 2026. ERCOT, The Solar Cliff, BESS Performance and Market, & Texas Energy Fund

This is about ERCOT solar and BESS resources, weather, time, and the dispatch stack on August 23, 2026. 

ERCOT Capacity:
**Thermal Capacity (Natural Gas, Coal, Nuclear, and others): ~87.4 GW
**Renewables & Storage (Wind, Solar, and Battery Energy Storage Systems): ~84.1 GW

ERCOT is structured as an energy-only market. There is no centralized capacity payment and no guaranteed revenue for being available.
Thus, assets are paid based solely on merit, market constraints, bidding strategies, and the dispatch stack.

The Event: Solar Cliff and BESS
On August 23, 2026, ERCOT reached a record weekend peak demand of 90,411 MW. 
Peak demand accounted for approximately 79.3% to 80.0% of ERCOT's total available system capacity (113,000 to 114,000 MW during that period).

Key Grid Metrics for August 23, 2026
Weekend Peak Demand Record: 90,411 MW (unofficial settlement)
Estimated System Capacity: ~113,000 – 114,000 MW (excluding ancillary services)
Ancillary services are now co-optimized in the Real Time Market
Weather Conditions and Grid Performance: Low wind output (~6,700 MW)  during high-temperature afternoon hours
Solar’s contribution (~33,000 MW) and battery      storage kept the grid stable without requiring any energy emergency alerts or conservation appeal

Solar Cliff and Weather and Time:
During the day on August 23, 2026, massive utility-scale solar generation carried a significant portion of the Texas grid's ~90 GW peak load. However, as solar generation rapidly ramped down in the late afternoon (the "solar cliff"), the grid faced a compounding reliability challenge:

*Wind Generation Shortfall: Wind came in significantly under forecast, providing over 2.5 GW less than what was anticipated during Day-Ahead Market (DAM) clearing.
*Extreme Demand: High temperatures kept air conditioning load sustained at near-record levels late into the evening. 

What happened with BESS
As solar exited the resource mix and wind underperformed, ERCOT had to rely on its ancillary service stack, particularly ECRS (which requires resources to respond within 10 minutes) and standard regulation services to maintain the grid's frequency.
Battery Discharge Peak: Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)—many of which carry ECRS      obligations—discharged heavily to fill the gap left by solar and wind.   Total battery discharge on the grid peaked at 19:50 (7:50 PM). 
The Price Peak Lag: Because ECRS and battery capacity have finite durations (often 1 to 2 hours), the grid's State of Charge (SoC) began running lower later into      the evening. Consequently, real-time electricity prices actually peaked at      21:00 (9:00 PM)more than an hour after battery discharge had      already peaked—as economic dispatch moved higher up to the thermal offer stack.

The bidding changes that allow rapid responsiveness to weather: ERCOT officially went live with Real-Time Co-optimization Plus Batteries (RTC+B) on December 5, 2025.  RTC+B allows ERCOT to simultaneously co-optimize energy and ancillary services every five minutes in real-time, while better modeling battery storage resources and their available states of charge. (Prior to December 5, 2025, ancillary services bids were set in the Day Ahead Market (DAM).

Behind the fence thermal or BESS resources usually do not count as ERCOT Capacity. Grid connected resources meeting NERC Standards may be too rough for large loads such as the manufacture of chips or may require batteries install inside the fence on the distribution side. Those batteries do not count as ERCOT resources unless they are also hooked up to provide ancillary services to ERCOT.
• It is said that batteries may replace gas-fired peakers. That may be. One constraint is that a single battery will have a discharge time of perhaps 3 hours, with state of charge factors intervening, while a peaker may be able to run indefinitely. But just like peakers, batteries can be arrayed in parallel to mimic expanded run time. Example connect two 12V 100Ah batteries in parallel create a 12V 200Ah system, doubling your runtime.
(Check with Grok)

Texas Energy Fund
But counteracting that, we have the Texas Energy Fund (PURA §25.510. Texas Energy Fund)
In-ERCOT Generation Loan Program.  largely to supply data centers. Natural gas peakers are experiencing a significant comeback in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) grid. This momentum is largely driven by a massive influx of data center interconnections and new financing options from the Texas Energy Fund (TEF). 

I do not see anything about the Texas Energy Fund loan peakers that enable them to handle the fragility of chips plants as well as batteries can provide service. I also do not know whether the Texas Energy Fund loan will be treated as a proxy for a capacity payment, thereby undermining batteries.

Section 1 — Market Snapshot

A toxic confluence of geopolitical supply shocks and stubborn wholesale inflation battered U.S. financial assets on Thursday, September 10, 2026, sending equities lower for a fourth consecutive trading session. Escalating conflict in the Middle East sparked a dramatic rally in energy benchmarks, pushing domestic crude back above triple digits. The resulting surge in long-dated sovereign yields triggered broad multiple compression across growth equities and heavy cyclical industrials, while defensive healthcare offered a rare pocket of stability.

The primary driver of market anxiety was the explosive move in the energy complex alongside an aggressive selloff in U.S. Treasuries. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude surged +6.72% to settle at $102.48 per barrel (touching intraday highs of $104.33/bbl), while Brent crude pushed past $107–$108/bbl amid severe disruptions to Middle Eastern transit lanes. Simultaneously, the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield leaped 11.0 basis points to settle at 4.950%—marking its highest closing level of the year after tapping an intraday peak of 4.970%. The policy-sensitive 2-year yield rose even faster, climbing 12.2 basis points to 4.548%. 

The central question dominating institutional desks and retail forums alike is whether this simultaneous spike in oil and yields represents an insurmountable stagflationary bind for financial assets. Rather than acting as an inflation hedge, spot gold fell 1.20% to $4,350.00/oz under the weight of rising real yields and a firmer U.S. dollar, while Bitcoin slid 1.30% to $77,330.00 (flirting with intraday lows near $76,950). On r/wallstreetbets, traders voiced growing alarm over tech's vulnerability: *"another leg up for oil and yields, while tech just pretends inflation doesn't exist until the Fed drops the hammer,"* wrote one user, while another observed, *"High oil plus 5% on the 10-year is about to cook this market. Puts printing tomorrow if CPI comes in hot too."* 

As Wall Street trading desks pointed out, when the risk-free rate flirts with 5% against a backdrop of triple-digit oil, equity valuations have virtually no room to absorb operational or macroeconomic misses. This vulnerability was acutely visible in high-beta tech, with the Invesco QQQ Trust dropping -1.07%, alongside sharp drops in semiconductor mainstays such as Intel (INTC down -5.70% to $23.40) and raw materials giant Freeport-McMoRan (FCX down -7.30% to $44.18). Conversely, defensive capital rotated selectively into regulated healthcare, lifting Elevance Health (ELV up +4.10% to $422.30) as management pointed to medical cost ratio stabilization.

San Salvador Preschool - Colton, Calif.

“Colton: The school district’s adult education program offers “Mommy and Me,” a program for children ages 2 through 5 and their parents. Classes meet from 8 to 11: 30 a.m. or noon to 3 p.m. Cost: $21 for materials, $4 registration. Information: (909) 876-4196. The San Salvador Child Development Center offers monthly classes covering topics such as child management skills, helping your child with academic skills and activities to do at home with your child.

“Where to find parent classes in S.B. County,” The San Bernardino County Sun (San Bernardino, CA), February 9, 1998, A4.

—

San Salvador Preschool in Colton was, in the late 1990s, the main early-childhood site for the Colton Joint Unified School District. It sat at 471 Agua Mansa Road, in the old Agua Mansa / San Salvador neighborhood just south of San Bernardino. By 1997–99 the official CDE “school” listing from the 1980s had already been closed, so the place usually appeared in directories and licensing records as the CJUSD / San Salvador Children’s Center. Families still called it “San Salvador Preschool.” The same building had been licensed as a child-development center since 1979.

The program served children ages 3–5 through California State Preschool and Head Start, with special-education preschool classes on site as well. Eligibility for the state and federal slots was income-based. The center was the district’s hub: some classrooms ran at San Salvador itself, while other State Preschool groups were housed at elementary campuses in Colton and Bloomington. The main phone number in that period was (909) 876-4240.

The program that operated there in 1997–99 is the same one that still exists at the site today. https://t.co/fOY0Pa7ZTu

text:
My mother is one of the unsung heroes of 9/11.

She worked a few blocks away from the WTC. When the planes hit and the buildings fell it shook her building- she said it felt like an earthquake, and it sounded like all the alarms in the city started going off. Everyone ran to the windows or down to the lobby to see what was happening, and then they saw the people. People were running by en masse, panicked, covered in soot and dust and gore. 

My mother was not in charge of the building; she was not even in charge of her office, but she took charge, because that’s the kind of person she is. She organized security to start evacuating the building, but she also told everyone to grab every cup, vase, pitcher, coffee pot- anything that could hold water- fill them and bring them down to the lobby as they left the building.

She stayed. A few security guards stayed with her, and they doused people with water as they ran by, gave them water to drink, brought them inside the lobby to rest for a moment, bandaged obvious wounds with what little medical supplies they had, and just helped whomever they could in whatever way they could. My mom gave away almost all her clothes: her suit jacket, her blouse, and her skirt. She only kept her shoes because her feet are so tiny no one fit into them. 

Late in the afternoon, after most of the dust settled and the crush of panicked people fleeing slowed to a trickle, the police came around and made my mom and the security guards leave the building. My mom walked in her slip and camisole and size 5 heels to one of the last boats that left the harbor and landed in New Jersey. She hitched a ride to the nearest train station that had a train going to Connecticut- the stranger that offered her a ride drove her quite a ways- and she finally stumbled through the front door of our house a bit after 10pm. 

The entire day she had no idea if my dad was okay. He was supposed to have breakfast with his sister at Windows that morning at 8am. My mom didn’t know that my dad decided to drive into the city that day- she left well before him- and got stuck in traffic. She didn’t know that his sister had overslept for the first time in her life. She had no idea where they were, but still she stayed as long as she could to help as many people as she could on the most devastating day of our lives. 

She’s only told the story once. I know she saw things that day that she doesn’t want to remember, and things she doesn’t want to forget. She lost a lot of friends and colleagues that day, as too many of us did. She doesn’t want recognition- she doesn’t think she did anything special- but I disagree. I count her among the thousands of unsung heroes of 9-11. 

Never forget.

text:
Harvesting Grace, A Forty-Day Devotional by C.S. McDonald is a warm, reflective Christian devotional that invites readers to slow down and reconnect with God’s grace, especially during the beauty of autumn.

Inspired by the author’s love of the fall season—with its vibrant colors, crisp air, and sense of harvest and gratitude—the book offers forty days of gentle spiritual nourishment. Each entry includes a daily Bible verse, a peaceful and thought-provoking observation, and soft reflections designed to refresh faith and cultivate joy. McDonald encourages readers to pause amid life’s busyness, sit quietly or take a walk, and intentionally harvest God’s steadfast love and boundless grace. It serves as a humble, encouraging guide that can be used in autumn or anytime throughout the year. Readers looking for a calming, faith-centered companion will find it uplifting and accessible.

Buy links
- Amazon (Kindle ebook): [https://t.co/T3ipW1VfVZ](https://t.co/T3ipW1VfVZ)
- Also check Amazon and other retailers for paperback or additional formats as they become available.

About the author
C.S. McDonald taught dance and choreographed shows for twenty-six years before turning to writing. She lives with her husband Bill and their dogs on a Thoroughbred farm near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. She is the author of the popular clean Fiona Quinn Mysteries (cozy mysteries featuring a kindergarten teacher turned sleuth) and the Owl’s Nest Mysteries, as well as children’s books inspired by farm life. In recent years she has added devotionals, including *Harvesting Grace*, as part of her spiritual writing. She is a wife, mom, grandma, dog lover, and self-described helpless chocoholic.

text:
The Taliban spent nearly two decades fighting the United States. Five years after returning to power in Kabul, it is now asking Washington to come back—but not with troops. The Taliban wants diplomatic relations, the reopening of the U.S. embassy, and American investment in Afghanistan’s mining, infrastructure, agriculture and trade sectors.

But there is an important distinction: Washington has not agreed to return. The Taliban is making the offer because it wants to break Afghanistan’s economic and diplomatic isolation and gain access to Western investment and frozen financial assets. The U.S. has so far rejected its proposal for American involvement in Afghanistan’s critical-minerals sector.

The irony is striking: the Taliban succeeded in forcing the United States out militarily, but five years later it is asking the same former enemy for something entirely different—diplomatic recognition, investment, technology and economic engagement. Winning a war against a foreign army is one thing; building a functioning economy and state after the war is another.

text:
*India: Not an Inspiration...but a Warning*

*Japan, a nation decimated by two nuclear bombs, didn't beg for sympathy or aid. It rebuilt itself with pride and an unshakeable sense of self-respect*. In the years since, it has never once stretched out a hand to America for alms.

An Indian man living in Japan for over a decade was about to leave Japan for good. He observed during his stay that no Japanese ever discussed or asked him much about India!

So, he had been a bit curious and asked his closest Japanese friend prior to departure: *What Japanese think about India & Indians in general?*

After a long pause, the friend replied, 
*"We are taught Indian history... not for inspiration, but as a warning."*

Confused, the Indian man asked, "A warning?"

"*Tell me," the Japanese friend continued, "how many British ruled India?"*
The Indian man thought, "Perhaps... around 10,000?"
The Japanese man nodded grimly. "And how many Indians lived there? Over 300 million, right?"
"Then who oppressed your people? Who carried out the orders to whip, torture, and shoot them?" he pressed. 

"*When General Dyer gave the command 'Fire!*' *at Jallianwala Bagh, who pulled the trigger?* The soldiers weren't British; they were Indian."
"Not one turned their rifle on the tyrant. Not one," he said. "*You want to talk about slavery? That was your real slavery. Not of the body, but of the soul."*

The Indian man stood frozen, silent, and ashamed.

*The Japanese friend went on, "How many Mughals came from Central Asia? A few thousand maybe?* And yet they ruled you for centuries. They built empires not with their numbers, but because *your own people bowed their heads and offered their loyalty in exchange for survival... or silver."*

"*Your own people converted. Your own brothers became instruments of their oppression. Your own men handed over your heroes*. Chandrashekhar Azad was betrayed. Bhagat Singh faced the gallows without even a whisper of help from those who called themselves patriots," he said.

"*You don't need foreign enemies. YOUR OWN PEOPLE BETRAY YOU AGAIN AND AGAIN FOR POWER, POSITION, AND PERSONAL GAIN. That is why we keep our distance.*"

"*When the British came to Hong Kong and Singapore, not one native man joined their army. But in India, you didn’t just join the enemy. You served them.* Worshipped them. Killed your own people to please them."

"*Even today, you haven’t changed*. Offer some free electricity, a bottle of liquor, a blanket—and your vote, your conscience, your voice are all sold without a second thought. *YOUR LOYALTY LIES NOT WITH YOUR NATION, BUT WITH YOUR STOMACH*," he said.

"You chant slogans. You march in protests. But when the country needs your character, where are you? YOUR FIRST LOYALTY IS STILL TO YOURSELF AND YOUR FAMILY. EVERYTHING ELSE —SOCIETY, DHARMA, THE COUNTRY —CAN BURN."

*He ended with one final statement:*
"If your nation is not strong, your home will never be safe. If your character is weak, no flag can protect you."

*This is not mockery. It is a mirror.*

Perhaps the time has come for us to stop looking away, because India doesn’t need more patriots in speeches. *IT NEEDS CITIZENS OF UNSHAKEABLE CHARACTER. NOT JUST FREEDOM FIGHTERS, BUT FREEDOM KEEPERS. NOT JUST FLAGS IN OUR HANDS, BUT LOYALTY IN OUR HEARTS*.

It is bitter. But it is true.

HOPE IT Shakes our conscience.

text:
The decadent people of the West are beginning to realize—far too late—that Christianity is the only religion compatible with the free-market economy, and therefore with political liberalism (Rom. 1:1–6, 1 Pet. 2:13–14). Indeed, civic liberty is the political counterpart to the theological concept of the dignity of humanity, glorified by God (John 1:14, 2 Peter 1:4), as are social equality and baptismal equality (Col. 3:11, Gal. 3:28), not to mention the Decalogue’s prohibition against theft (Ex. 20:1–17).  

Capitalism, however, is based on three principles without which no fair exchange is possible: the freedom and equality of individuals, as well as the right to property. Consequently, neither the slave-holding and misogynistic forms of Judaism and Islam, nor Hinduism with its ritual killings of widows or its caste system, nor contemplative Buddhism, nor—even less so—totalitarian communism and its trail of millions of deaths, are compatible with the civilization emerging from capitalism: the least inhumane known in this world.  

As such, it would be better to stop persecuting the Church and to promote the “modus vivendi” that laïcité offers between ideologies—whether sacred or secular—and the impartiality of the state and its employees, while taking care not to import too large a contingent of mindsets contrary to civilization.
